title: CLAUDE.md section 8 bans the one hybrid every prefab is built from
claim: The section 8 dead-end 'Real content through a synthetic frame is still synthesis' contradicts the working record. Rung F (a verbatim core in a minted frame), world-mountain and world-forest (rigid real rock or canopy carried onto a MINTED island), and both catalog prefabs are all real content in a synthetic frame. Every case the line was minted from deformed the real content PER VERTEX or REPAINTED it: the v3 bend-carry's ribbon reparameterization with wander, top-snap and foot fix-ups, and the dunes label-stamp, which kept row labels and threw away the mesh. Every rigid or smooth-global-affine carry passes: rotation at any angle, spread to x1.5, rock-height to x2, de-tilt. The real law is 'per-vertex reparameterization or label repaint of real content fails; a rigid or declared smooth global map passes'.
laws_involved: section 8 'real content through a synthetic frame'
evidence: CLAUDE.md:243-244 states the line unqualified. SYNTHESIS-RECONSIDERED.md:72-74 ('A section 8 line that mis-summarizes') already flags it. rockstretch/NOTES.md:87 shows the blend-conform smear (an uneven per-vertex pull) 'stays refuted' while the pure-Y scale passed. desert-peak-isle (a carried, turned peak on a minted r60 island) was owner-walked (PREFABS.md:113-117). KIT POLICY plus PLAYTEST VERDICT; the passing cases are in-game proven.
proposed_action: Rewrite the section 8 line in place: 'Real content deformed per vertex (ribbon or bend warp, local conform) or reduced to labels repainted on a synthetic grid is still synthesis. A rigid or declared smooth global map of the whole mesh is a carry.' Keep both falsifications as its evidence.
cheapest_test: None needed; this is a wording fix. Sanity check: list every owner-passed carry-on-mint (Rung F, Uaho/crag/comp20/desert-peak, the five canopies, desert-peak-isle) and confirm none used a per-vertex warp.
risk: Low. Over-loosening could re-open per-vertex warps, so the rewrite must keep 'per-vertex' explicitly banned.

verdict.reason: The contradiction is real, and the record already names it. SYNTHESIS-RECONSIDERED.md:72-82 quotes the section 8 line and says the bend-carry failed because it WARPED real bytes, that a RIGID carry in a synthesized frame is the Rung F architecture that worked, and that 'the section 8 line as written forbids the one hybrid that works'. verdict.corrected_claim: The section 8 line is already flagged as a mis-summary in SYNTHESIS-RECONSIDERED but is still uncorrected in CLAUDE.md. title: THE FORM LESSON is scoped as 'rock synthesis is dead', but the killing defect was an undecoded junction that later beat a CARRIED massif too
claim: massif_synth's 8 rounds are cited as proof that rock organization cannot be synthesized. By the record, the face-window mechanics were approved in game mid-arc ('cuts are clean and density looks nice'), and the arc died at the grass/rock FOOT transition. That defect class later defeated a CARRIED massif (R4 west-seam, 0 for 12) until the BAND-CONTINUATION, LAWN-LINE and PROFILE laws were decoded. None of those laws existed when massif_synth ran. The falsification therefore covers 'synthetic massif with an invented foot, on one r26 grass islet, without the render or peer gates', not 'synthetic massif face'. Meanwhile the synthesis that passes (world-island coast columns, mains, hill, relief, world-water, THE SPUR, THE TUCK) shares one property: low-dimensional or no 3D massing to invent, built from the neighbour's own vocabulary.
evidence: Map reader 1 cites memory project-ff9-overworld-interior-topography.md:481-545 (8 rounds, 2026-07-13, bench (2,19), seed 42). The foot laws are dated later (BASE-TILE-GRAMMAR 2026-07-31; lawn-line 2026-10-07; PROFILE LAW from the R4 arc). SYNTHESIS-RECONSIDERED.md:27: 'Isolation was the default condition of every synthesis failure, not the missing ingredient.' CLAUDE.md:238-239 states the ban without that scope. PLAYTEST VERDICT measured on one bench; applied project-wide.
proposed_action: Re-scope the section 8 entry to what was tested: an invented cone/ridge massing with an invented foot, one islet, pre-foot-laws, no pixel or peer gate. State the generalization the record does support: synthesis passes where stock's own massing is low-dimensional, using constants measured on the immediate neighbour. Leave synthetic massif faces as an OPEN cell, not a dead end.
cheapest_test: Register one prediction: the v3 face-window mechanics (continuous-flow UV, smooth-field law, Moguri-safe inset windows) on a donor's carried SILHOUETTE, joined to a carried comp20-style foot (no authored foot), judged first by the render and peer gates offline. Deploy only if both are green, then one owner look.
risk: Medium. The FORM LESSON may still hold (DEFECT FOLLOWS AUTHORSHIP predicts a new defect on the new face). Cost is one registered round. Benefit: new massif shapes beyond 7 donors.

verdict.reason: Several parts check out. The memory confirms that the window mechanics were approved mid-arc ('cuts are clean and density looks nice'), and that rounds 7-8 died on the foot/grass boundary ('confused about where the grass goes', 'patchwork') (project-ff9-overworld-interior-topography.md:530-545). The R4 arc confirms that a carried massif's minted foot then failed 0 for 12, and that the PROFILE/BAND-CONTINUATION laws came later (ground-junction-synthesis.md:99-125). So the 8-round test did not isolate 'synthetic face' from 'invented foot'. The analyst misses wider counter-evidence that keeps the face cell closed, not open. Rounds 1 and 2 and v3 round 1 failed on the FACE itself ('no upward grain', 'very warped and stretched'), not the foot. SYNTHESIS-RECONSIDERED.md:64-66 still names massif flanks as the continuous-flow class that 'FAILS every time'. Re-minted rock texture beside carried rock failed in game on the mesa base ('mismatched faces', MESA-CARRY-PREDICTION.md:84-100). The proposed test is synthetic face windows on a carried silhouette. That is minted texture on carried form, the exact mechanism the mesa fringe re-mint lost on. DEFECT FOLLOWS AUTHORSHIP predicts the defect lands on that minted face.
verdict.corrected_claim: The massif_synth falsification confounds face and foot. The face mechanics were owner-approved at round ~5, after earlier face failures, and the arc died on an invented foot before the foot laws existed. Scoping section 8 to 'invented massing + invented foot, one islet' is fair. Wider evidence (the SYNTHESIS-RECONSIDERED category split; the mesa base re-mint failing beside carried faces) still argues against minted rock-face texture next to carried rock. Treat a registered face-window-on-carried-silhouette round as a high-risk, FORM-LESSON-exposed bet, not an open cell the record leans toward.

title: The terrace-wall refutation rests on a confounded build and a mis-decoded reference wall

(1) The builder terrace_wall_t1.py keys cells as int(-cz//4). terrace_wall_strip.py later root-caused exactly that key as THE 'BANDED TOP' (mains decode 0/354 with it, 59/60 fixed). So the mains were NOT lawful, and lesson 2 is misattributed; it also contradicts the many flat mints that pass (island E, the r52 desert, desert-peak-isle). (2) uvclass shows the (14,13) reference wall is only 29.6% W.keyed and 64.3% M.flow, so the 'tile language' target was mostly a continuous-flow object: the decode's grouping cut charts at tile lines. The remaining four named defect classes still stand, so 'invented massing fails' survives, but 'faithfully implemented' does not.
evidence: Confirmed by reading: terrace_wall_t1.py:909-915 returns (int(cx4 // CELL), int(-cz4 // CELL)). terrace_wall_strip.py:2344-2351 says 'The negated int(-z//4) convention ... every u collapsed (THE ROUND-3 BANDED TOP ... decode rate 0/354 with the negated key, 59/60 with this one)'. TERRACE-WALL-PREDICTION.md:109 calls round 2 'terrace_wall_t1.py round 3 internally', and :129 says 'A dead-flat shelf bands even under lawful mains'. uvclass/NOTES.md:73 gives the (14,13) wall as '64.3% M.flow, 29.6% W.keyed ... (recorded "tile language": see R3)'.
proposed_action: Annotate TERRACE-WALL-PREDICTION SCORED round 2: the banded top was plumbing, so strike lesson 2, and note the reference wall's real class mix. Change section 8 to 'refuted on four of five named classes; banded top was a cell-key bug'.
cheapest_test: Offline only: rebuild round 2 with the floor-z key, re-run the mains decode-rate check and the offline renderer, and see which of 'obvious tiling' and 'grass-cliff tiling mid-wall' survive.

verdict.reason: Both confounds are confirmed, and both are already recorded elsewhere. terrace_wall_t1.py:909-915 keys cells int(-cz//4). terrace_wall_strip.py:2344-2351, STRIP-CARRY-PREDICTION.md:100-103 and :144 root-cause round 3's 'banded grass on top' as that key ('confirmed fixed in-game, both playtests'). Re-word to 'refuted for the DECODED (partly mis-decoded) language on four of five named defect classes; banded top = plumbing'.

title: Normals are an engine-inert channel, yet kit docstrings still call them part of the language and say the engine lights with them

Any synthesis cost model, or any defect diagnosis that blames normals, is pointed at a mechanism the engine does not read. CLAUDE.md section 7 itself warns about this.
laws_involved: WALL MESH ORGANIZATION law 3 (flat washed lighting)
evidence: grassland.py:682-685 (read): 'Real grass normals are smoothed geometric -- never (0,1,0); the engine lights with them'. interior.py:27-30 (read): '...with LOCAL normal re-smoothing'. GROUND-JUNCTION-SYNTHESIS.md:206-211 (read): 'binds only vertex + texcoord ... Round 8's entire lighting half of the seam pass could not change a single pixel ... never spend another round on ground shading'. CLAUDE.md:211-212. Normals are harmless to KEEP (the prefab fingerprint rounds them at 1e-6), but they are not language.
proposed_action: Correct both docstrings: normals are written for byte-faithfulness and for the Falls/Stream shaders only, and are render-inert on Terrain. Drop 'normal re-smoothing' from the hill-language bullet. Credit the Uaho v3.2 'stale normals' fix to the clamp revert it was bundled with.
cheapest_test: Doc edit. If a skeptic wants proof: offline renderer A/B of one island with all Terrain normals set to (0,1,0); expect identical pixels.
risk: Very low

verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading. grassland.py:682-685 says 'the engine lights with them and the dapple masks tile borders'. interior.py:27-30 lists 'LOCAL normal re-smoothing' inside THE GRASS-HILL LANGUAGE. GROUND-JUNCTION-SYNTHESIS.md:206-211 states the engine fact (Terrain binds only vertex + texcoord; WMMesh.Normals has zero non-debug readers; the walk recomputes geometrically; 'never spend another round on ground shading'). water.py's header says the same for water. title: The hill's 2.4u 'flat host' guard silently disables hills on relief islands, and the relief exclusivity rule is a docstring wish
claim: world-hill's lawful() refuses any footprint whose raw y-span exceeds 2.4u. Its own comment justifies this with 'a plain mint is flat'. That premise is false on a --relief island. Measured here on the shipped grassland.relief at amp 1.3, without the rim fade: the raw span exceeds 2.4u on 14% of r14 footprints, 26% of r20 and 67% of r30. So a hill lands only where the noise happens to be calm, and the guard cannot tell ambient relief from a prior hill. Meanwhile build_landmass's docstring declares relief 'MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE' with hill/forest/mountain and names the 2.4u gate as 'the backstop'. That gate exists only in the hill, so nothing enforces exclusivity for forest or mountain carves. Both rules also push every carried feature onto a flat host, which S5 measures as only the ~10% calm-host subpopulation of stock; stock features sit on the regional ground field.
laws_involved: A law in a docstring is a wish (CLAUDE.md section 7)
evidence: interior.py:1386-1390 (read): '...a plain mint is flat ... if float(tri_cy[sel].max() - tri_cy[sel].min()) > 2.4: return None'. island.py:392-393 (read): 'Relief is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with the explicit-height verbs per island (the ROLLING-RELIEF ENVELOPE 2.4u gate is the backstop)'. Read-only run (scratchpad cx/span.py, 200 random sites per radius): grass amp 1.3 r14 p50 1.84 / p90 2.51 / 14% >2.4; r20 p50 2.10 / 26%; r30 p50 2.58 / 67%. Desert x1.6 r20: 97%. GROUND-JUNCTION-SYNTHESIS.md:224-235: calm hosts are 17 of 176. KIT POLICY measured on flat mints (island E) and applied to relief mints it predates.
proposed_action: Replace the raw-span test with a DETRENDED one: the residual of tri y over land_height + relief_fade*relief(x,z) at the island's own frame and seed, or over a local plane fit. That still refuses stacking on a prior hill but admits ambient relief. Then decide explicitly, in code, whether forest and mountain carves may sit on relief (their aprons and zips read lifted ground), and either enforce or delete the 'mutually exclusive' sentence.
cheapest_test: Offline: mint a --relief --prefab-frame grass r60 island, run world-hill --dry-run scans with the current guard vs the detrended guard, and compare the accepted-site counts and the slope envelope of the result. In game: one prefab with relief + hill, walked once.
risk: Low for the hill: the slope and peak gates still bound it. Forest and mountain on relief are an unmeasured walk-junction risk and need their own single walk.

verdict.reason: Code confirmed: interior.py:1386-1390 has the raw y-span > 2.4 refusal with 'a plain mint is flat'. island.py:392-393 declares relief MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with hill/forest/mountain, with the 2.4u gate as the backstop. The same wording is in README.md:569-570 and the CHANGELOG. A grep finds no exclusivity enforcement anywhere else, so forest and mountain have no backstop. I re-ran the analyst's span.py and got the same numbers: grass amp 1.3 is over 2.4u on 14% / 26% / 67% of r14 / r20 / r30 footprints, desert x1.6 r20 on 97%. One nuance: by the design record (README.md:324-327, memory interior-topography:912-915), the 2.4u gate was minted on flat island E as an anti-STACKING guard, and was later reused as the relief backstop. So refusing hills on relief is the declared intent, and the gate enforces it only probabilistically. The real defect is that the declared exclusivity is a docstring wish ('A law in a docstring is a wish'): partial for the hill, absent for forest and mountain. The S5 'calm host 10%' link is a stretch (S5 is about feature approach ground, not hill hosts).
verdict.corrected_claim: Relief/height-verb exclusivity is declared, not enforced. The hill's 2.4u span gate, minted as an anti-stacking guard on flat island E, refuses only a radius-dependent fraction of relief footprints (reproduced: 14-67% for grass, ~all for desert). Forest and mountain carves have no gate at all. Either enforce exclusivity at the call site (refuse when the island row has relief_amp > 0), or replace the raw span with a detrended residual and measure relief-hosted carves with one walk each.

title: S5 convicts lift-with-falloff aprons; world-mountain ships exactly that apron on all 7 donors and it passes
claim: S5 (the one law that survived its skeptic) says stock feature feet sit on a lip then a LEVEL terrace about 1.0-1.5u over the lowland, never a monotone radial mound (0 of 176). GROUND-JUNCTION-SYNTHESIS concludes the next build 'is a deletion'. world-mountain's default seat is a pure-Y Shepard apron lift blended over MTN_GBLEND 12u, a monotone radial mound by construction, and it is owner-passed on Uaho, crag, comp20, desert peak and others. S5 was measured as a census but CONVICTED on one bench: a large carried wall on a flat Path-D host with a 4.4u weld-relief arrangement. Its scope is unstated. Either S5's conviction is scale- or class-specific (escarpment wall vs small lattice-sheet massif), or the shipped apron is a latent defect no walk has named yet. The foot laws J3 (level plain, 0.00 slope), S5 (1.0-1.5u terrace), the Uaho anatomy (~2.5u up a 20 deg shoulder) and the PROFILE LAW (a convex toe at 42-53 deg) all lack a class label.
laws_involved: THE ROCK-RIGID LAW (all seating deformation to the grass apron)
evidence: GROUND-JUNCTION-SYNTHESIS.md:229-231 (read): 'LIFT-with-falloff manufactures a monotone radial mound resolving back to a plane, of which stock has 0 instances in 176 components', and :413 'The next build's spec is therefore a deletion'. interior.py:97 (read): 'MTN_GBLEND = 12.0 # ground-apron blend reach'. interior.py:33-34: 'ALL seating deformation goes to the GRASS (the donor-shaped pure-Y apron lift)'. donors.toml lists 7 qualified massifs, all owner-passed (map reader 5).
proposed_action: Run one class-labelled foot census (escarpment wall vs lattice-sheet massif) that measures S5's distance-band offsets, J3 slope and the PROFILE kink per class. Restate S5 with the class it covers. If the shipped aprons are off-language for their class, record it as a known latent risk, not a gate.
cheapest_test: Offline: run S5's distance-band offset/slope metric (0-4/4-8/8-16/16-32u) on the written bytes of desert-peak-isle and two other qualified world-mountain benches, and compare against the 176-component stock distribution split by class.
risk: Low (measurement only). If it finds the aprons off-language, the honest output is a note, since owner verdicts outrank the census for already-walked pieces.

verdict.reason: The tension is real: GROUND-JUNCTION-SYNTHESIS.md:226-231 convicts lift-with-falloff (0 of 176), and :413 sets the next spec as 'a deletion'. interior.py:31-34 and :97 ship the pure-Y apron lift (MTN_GBLEND 12) on all qualified massifs. But it is partly already recognized: memory ground-junction-synthesis.md:116-123 says world-mountain 'is the PRE-Path-D Uaho pipeline (rock-only carry + apron lift + DP zip) and never absorbed Path D's answer -- THE FULL SKIRT ... no lift'. The R4 rejections all landed on its minted foot. The record also explains why aprons can pass: S5's conviction targets ARRANGEMENT, while the amplitude was 'in-language (~stock p80)' (:233-234), and the bench was a 4.4u weld-relief large wall. The class-labelled census is a new, cheap measurement and has not been done.
verdict.corrected_claim: S5 was measured as a stock census and convicted on one large-wall bench. world-mountain's apron lift is already recorded as the pre-Path-D pipeline that never absorbed THE FULL SKIRT, yet it passes on small qualified massifs. Run a class-labelled foot census (S5 bands, J3 slope, PROFILE kink) on the written bytes of qualified world-mountain benches versus stock by class, and restate S5's scope. Record any off-language aprons as known latent risk, since walks outrank the census.

title: THE ONE-SITE WORLD LAW is a stale occupancy scan stated as a permanent law

The scan behind it forbade every seam-crossing footprint because 'build_landmass REFUSES col<0'. That is no longer true: landmass() now canonicalizes the centre mod 1536 and wraps labels at the seam. The scan also counted every live-deployed block as occupied, and the owner reset the world map on 2026-11-08. It was measured for one donor size (R>=125). No kit code enforces it.
evidence: freshmint_site_scan.py:5-8 (read): '(b) every LIVE-DEPLOYED block ... (c) the x-wrap seam (the whole footprint stays inside [0,1536), build_landmass REFUSES col<0)'. island.py:1464-1468 and :1488-1492 (read): the centre is canonicalized and 'THE SEAM WRAP: both install-probing gates below MUST see the WRAPPED labels'. CLAUDE.md:296 (read). PREFABS.md:66-67 (read). PREFABS.md:113-114: the reset left 'all 30 stock windows free'. STOCK CENSUS, but of a past live map, with a now-lifted kit restriction.
proposed_action: Re-word section 10 to 'one R>=125 site on the July live map, seam excluded'. Do not ship max_per_world until the scan is re-run.
cheapest_test: Read-only: re-run freshmint_site_scan.py with clause (c) dropped (seam-wrapping footprints allowed) and clause (b) pointed at the post-reset live tree (only (9-11,8-10) occupied); report every R>=125 lattice centre.
risk: None for the scan. A second two-ground site, if found, still needs its own walk.

verdict.reason: freshmint_site_scan.py:1-14 does exclude seam-crossing footprints because 'build_landmass REFUSES col<0', and landmass() now canonicalizes the centre and wraps labels (island.py:1462-1492). So clause (c) is stale. The 'exactly one' figure, however, is stated in GROUND-FAMILY-DECODE:2418 as a STOCK-world fact: the one R>=125 site is the Rung F site itself, and the best fresh site is 115.38u vs 125.38u 'with antipodal blockers'. The world reset therefore does not create a second site; it only frees the original. Only the seam exclusion can change the count, so the analyst over-weights clause (b) and the reset. SYNTHESIS-RECONSIDERED.md:43 already calls the law 'pure occupancy'. Also, junction_compose is a study script (operators/NOTES.md:295), so seam-wrapping support there is unverified.
verdict.corrected_claim: THE ONE-SITE WORLD LAW is a stock-clearance count over NON-seam-crossing footprints. The reset frees the one site but adds none. Re-run the scan with clause (c) dropped, and check that junction_compose wraps at the seam, before stating 'exactly one'. Until then, word it as 'one non-seam R>=125 stock site'.

title: The open-ocean law probes the STOCK bundle, so 'make room with a sink' cannot work; its engine half covers only 15 blocks per disc
claim: PREFABS.md says a prefab on the live map 'needs room made first (a sink or a move)'. _real_block_parts reads the REAL disc's assets via transplant.world_tris, so a stock land block that world-sink has removed still holds stock parts and refuses every mint and prefab forever. Only moving or removing KIT land frees room. The law's own comment calls it 'a PROXY' for IsSea. Its two rationales differ in kind. 'A sea-only prefab has no Terrain transform' is an ENGINE FACT, but only for the ~15 water-only own-prefab blocks per disc. 'A land block would be shredded' is KIT POLICY: stock land blocks have a Terrain child that binds, and are edited in place routinely by morph_in_place, virgin_mint and world-terrain. The law is stated as a single engine-backed refusal.
evidence: island.py:1411-1423 (read): the probe iterates transplant.PARTS over world_tris(... disc ...) of the REAL game. island.py:1474-1484 (read): 'No escape hatch ... The law is a PROXY: it probes the REAL disc's per-block assets'. island.py:1502-1504 (read): the probe 'answers does the REAL game ship assets here -- a different question from is this target free'. PREFABS.md:109 (read): '(a sink or a move)'. consumption/NOTES.md section 4 (per map readers): coastal (8,17) binds Terrain, water-only (8,18) does not.
sources_to_check: memory project-ff9-overworld-coast-mosaic.md LAW INDEX B (THE OPEN-OCEAN TARGET LAW)
proposed_action: Fix PREFABS.md:109 to say 'a move of kit land'. Split the law in the docstring into its engine half (refuse water-only own-prefab blocks unless armed; the bind oracle) and its policy half (never author over a stock-owned block). Optionally add a live-state mode that admits a block the ledger shows the kit fully owns (sunk, every own-prefab part overridden), behind the PREFAB-PARTS gate, as a separate qualified lane.

verdict.corrected_claim: Marginal-statistic gates predicted 0 of 13 verdicts. In the next arc, pixel-rendered gates scored against owner-accepted peers caught 4 of 6 defects (one arc, small n). title: The coastline shape gate refuses large one-lobe islands because the generator does not scale, not because FF9 forbids them
claim: verify_landmass requires a median turn of at least 8 deg per 8u, a scale-invariant stock fact (coasts turn ~22 deg per 8u at every size). blob_outline's undulation is angular, frequencies 2-5 per revolution with amplitude ~1/f, so its turning per 8u falls as 1/R. A pure circle turns 458/R deg per 8u and crosses 8 deg near R~57, so large single masses fail. That forces multi-lobe outlines for the owner's 'new landmass' case and inflates footprints (THE LOBE-OVERSHOOT ERROR). multi_blob_outline already has a fixed-amplitude ripple term; blob_outline has none.
evidence: island.py:1147 (read): shape ok = 8.0 <= med_turn <= 35.0 and acute <= 0.12 and max_turn < 150. mesh.py:1147-1148 (read): comps for f in (2,3,4,5), 'amplitude ~1/f keeps it gentle'. mesh.py:1183-1185 (read): multi_blob adds a 'ripple' term. The 1/R turning is geometry (CALC: 8/R rad = 458/R deg). The r94 refusal is recorded in the terrain-malleability memory, round 21 (per map reader 4).
proposed_action: Add a radius-scaled 8u-scale ripple and dent rate to blob_outline (opt-in, so frozen identities hold), or let build_landmass take a real stock coast polyline, rigidly transformed, as its outline. That carries the silhouette, THE FORM LESSON's own carrier, and needs the prefab frame measured for custom outlines.
cheapest_test: Offline: sweep blob_outline r40-r120 over 20 seeds with and without a scaled ripple, and report outline_shape_stats pass rates. Then one walk of an r90 one-lobe mint.
risk: Low. A new outline is authored surface, so its look must be walked once.

verdict.reason: Verified by a read-only sweep (blob_outline vs the verify_landmass shape test at island.py:1147, 20 seeds per radius). One-lobe blob median turn per 8u falls 24.1 / 14.7 / 10.4 / 9.8 / 7.2 / 5.7 / 4.8 deg at R 24 / 40 / 57 / 60 / 80 / 100 / 120. The pass rate is 20/20 through R60 and 0/20 from R80 up. multi_blob_outline (base 0.7R) passes 19-20/20 at every radius, thanks to its 8u-scale ripple term (mesh.py:1183-1185; its comment says 'big radii need it'). blob_outline has no such term (mesh.py:1147-1148). verdict.corrected_claim: Single-lobe blob_outline fails the coastline shape gate at R of about 70-80 and above (measured: 0/20 at R80+), because its angular-frequency undulation turns as 1/R. multi_blob already passes at all radii via a ripple term. title: The hill's 2.4u raw y-span guard refuses ordinary rolling relief, which blocks relief plus carry prefabs
claim: The guard exists to stop a second hill stacking on a prior hill. It actually measures RAW footprint y-span, so it cannot tell ambient relief from a placed hill. With the shipped grassland.relief at the default amp 1.3, 26.5% of grass hill footprints (r18+2) exceed 2.4u, and 91.5% do at desert scale x1.6. That is a proxy guarding the wrong hazard. The 'relief is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with world-hill/forest/mountain' rule in the docstring has no code behind it for forest or mountain. It pushes every carried feature onto a flat host, although S5 measured stock calm hosts at only ~10% (17/176). Most stock features sit on a regional ground field.
laws_involved: THE RELIEF RESURRECTION (PLAYTEST VERDICT 'nice - gently rolling')
REAL GRASS IS NEVER FLAT (STOCK CENSUS)
evidence: interior.py:1380-1393: lawful() refuses when tri_cy[sel].max()-min() > 2.4. Its own comment says 'a plain mint is flat'. island.py:392-393 docstring: 'Relief is MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with the explicit-height verbs per island (the ... 2.4u gate is the backstop)'. My read-only sampling (scratch span.py, 400 random sites, footprint disc r20 at 2u spacing, G.relief amp 1.3*scale): grass p50 2.12 / p90 2.72 / max 3.57u, 26.5% over 2.4. Desert x1.6: p50 3.36, 91.5% over 2.4. GROUND-JUNCTION-SYNTHESIS.md:225-235 (0/176 pedestals; 17/176 calm hosts).
proposed_action: Replace the raw span with a DETRENDED residual. If the island was minted with relief, subtract grassland.relief at the island's own seed and frame. Otherwise subtract a local plane fit. Refuse when the residual span exceeds ~1.0u, which still catches a prior hill (prominence >= 2u). Then state a real rule for forest and mountain carves on a relief island: the apron and zip read lifted ground. Until that rule exists, drop the 'mutually exclusive' wording or enforce it in code.
cheapest_test: Offline, no install writes. (a) The residual test must refuse every footprint on island E's existing hill (positive control) and accept most sites on a relief mint (expect >95%). (b) Build one framed relief island + hill + forest prefab offline and check the verbs' own gates. (c) One owner walk of that candidate.
risk: A hill on relief adds two height fields, so flank slope can exceed MAX_FLANK where they align. The existing flank and peak gates still run on the summed surface. Forest and mountain aprons on a non-flat lawn are unmeasured, so the walk carries the risk.

verdict.reason: I confirmed the guard: lawful() refuses when the raw y-span of the footprint tris exceeds 2.4u, and its comment says 'a plain mint is flat'. The memory names the hazard it was minted for: a hill stacking on island E's hill, caught live as a 38.8 deg flank refusal. Its scope was a flat mint, not relief. I re-ran the analyst's span.py and got the same numbers: grass amp 1.3 p50 2.12 / p90 2.72 / 26.5% over 2.4; desert x1.6 p50 3.36 / 91.5% over 2.4. The relief verb is in-game proven ('nice - gently rolling'). The island.py docstring's 'MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with the explicit-height verbs' has no code behind it. A grep of interior.py finds no relief or host-flatness check in the forest or mountain carves; the hill's 2.4u gate is the only backstop. S5 confirms stock features sit on the regional ground field, with 0/176 pedestals. Its 'calm host' class (17/176) is itself defined as ground spanning <=4.15u within 50.6u, which is far looser than 2.4u over r20. One limit: span.py samples the noise field on a disc, not the mint's triangles, and ignores the 2-12u shore fade. That is close enough for a proxy argument.
verdict.corrected_claim: The 2.4u raw-span gate was minted on FLAT mints to stop hill-on-hill stacking (island E). Applied to an opt-in relief mint, it refuses ~26% of grass and ~92% of desert footprints for ambient noise rather than a prior hill. The docstring's 'mutually exclusive' rule is enforced only for world-hill, and only by this proxy. Forest and mountain carves on a relief island are neither refused nor measured.

title: Whole-block placement snap is an artifact of a block-anchored frame and a triangle fingerprint, not a property of the land
claim: 'A 4u or 32u shift is different land' was measured as different TRIANGLES. Two of the three frame anchors (relief and the mountain hash) sit at the corner of the block holding the centre, so a sub-block shift necessarily reads different noise. The decal shuffle is sorted, so translation preserves its order. Block borders are multiples of 64 and so already lie on the 4u lattice that the cell-clipped mains, the lip and the stamps are cut on. If the frame were anchored at a 4u lattice point, a 0-mod-4 shift might change only how tris are split at block borders: the same piecewise surface, uv and topo. The engine reads that surface per block (THE BLOCK LAW), not the fingerprint. Placement freedom would rise from 1 to 16 offsets per axis per block.
laws_involved: THE WHOLE-BLOCK PREFAB SHIFT LAW (KIT POLICY, measured as triangle identity)
evidence: island.py:449-451: frame_x = BLOCK*floor(cx/BLOCK). PREFABS.md table: 4u and 32u give 'different land (the block/cell clip moves)', and the relief mint 'still differs at 32u (the control)'. That control differs because the frame did not move with the land. prefab.py:21-25 hashes triangles. uvclass LAWFUL DEFORMATIONS: L.rule 'XZ translate 0-mod-4 exact'.
proposed_action: Add an opt-in 4u-anchored frame (origin = the 4u lattice point nearest the centre, relief and hash keyed from it). Add a SURFACE fingerprint beside the triangle one: dense samples of (y, uv, topo, walk class) at fixed relative points, plus first-hit order where sheets overlap. Admit 4u offsets only where the surface fingerprint matches.
cheapest_test: Offline only. With the 4u anchor, build the desert-peak-isle at offsets 4, 16 and 32u, then compare surface samples and the placement census (MISS==0, cast traps at block-cut lines). This needs no install and no walk unless it passes.
risk: Re-clipping at a new block border can create lattice-edge teleport traps (barycentric 0 hits) and changes which block answers the query along the seam. The Sea4 cut and coastnav stamp are per block and may not be surface-identical. The footprint can also touch an extra block, which then needs to be clear. If any of these differ, keep the whole-block snap.

verdict.reason: I confirmed the frame is block-anchored (frame_x = BLOCK*floor(cx/BLOCK)). The mains are translation-invariant by construction: assign_mains draws over the whole island's SORTED cells, and mains_uv is cell-local. I then ran a stronger read-only test than the PREFABS one, sampling surfaces instead of triangles. build_landmass grass r30 lobes 2 and desert r40 (no relief, no decals) were shifted 4u, 32u and 64u. At 3000 random relative points, the barycentric (y, u, v) of every covering triangle was IDENTICAL: 0 differing points out of 807 and 1427 surfaced points. The triangle multisets differ by 19-43 tris, mostly ones that touch a 64u block border. So PREFABS' '4u, 32u: different land (the block/cell clip moves)' is a triangle-split artifact for the plain mint. The relief control differs only because the frame did not move. Not checked: idall/topo, walk classes, the Sea4 cut and coastnav stamp, and lattice-edge cast traps at the new border cuts.
citations: scratchpad v/surf.py and v/x4.py (my runs: 0 surface differences at 4u/32u/64u)
verdict.corrected_claim: For the plain mint, a 4u or 32u shift is the SAME surface (y and uv identical at 3000 sampled points). It is not the same triangle list, because the block-border splits move. With a 4u-anchored frame for relief and the mountain hash, plus a surface fingerprint, sub-block placement looks feasible. Topo, sea, coastnav and border cast traps still need the same check.

title: THE ONE-SITE WORLD LAW is a stale July occupancy scan that excluded the x seam, quoted as a permanent law

title: The open-ocean target law probes the STOCK bundle, so land the kit has sunk can never host a mint or prefab
claim: _real_block_parts reads stock world_tris, not the live map. A stock block that world-sink removed, or that is otherwise dead in the live stack, still refuses forever. laws_involved: THE OPEN-OCEAN TARGET LAW (KIT POLICY; its own comment calls it a PROXY)
evidence: island.py:1411-1424: _real_block_parts iterates transplant.world_tris over stock. island.py:1458-1471: 'The law is a PROXY: it probes the REAL disc's per-block assets to infer IsSea'. consumption/NOTES.md:45-46,175-176: coastal (8,17) binds Terrain; water-only (8,18) has 'Terrain (dead even when present)'. (2) A POLICY gate: refuse when STOCK land is LIVE at the block, judged after the FolderNames stack (a sunk or blanked block passes). A non-IsSea host must also override every child of the block's own prefab (Sea1/2/3/5, Object) so no stock shore ring free-rides. Add the bound-part set to the prefab fingerprint so the walk's context identity survives.
cheapest_test: Offline: run the bind oracle (render.effective_prefab / predict_reads) on a block sunk by world-sink with a staged prefab, and confirm every bound child is overridden or blanked. Then one walk of a prefab on a sunk island's former blocks.

The 'one walk qualifies every site' argument then needs the bound-part set in the fingerprint. Disc 4 may still have the stock land (THE TWO-TREE LAW), so the sink must exist on both trees.

verdict.reason: Confirmed: _real_block_parts iterates transplant.world_tris over the STOCK bundle. A block that world-sink (which sinks REAL islands) has already turned to water therefore still refuses forever, and the code's own comment calls the law a PROXY. consumption NOTES section 4 confirms that a non-IsSea block binds its OWN prefab, with Donor.txt dead there. PREFABS' 'sink or move' is ambiguous: the room there was taken by KIT overrides on stock open ocean, and freeing those passes the gate. Only a world-sink of real land runs into this contradiction. An inland block may lack Sea3/4/5 children entirely, and the mint's Terrain + cut Sea4 + blank Sea1/2/3/5 schema would then not bind, leaving holes. An engine-true replacement must use the bind oracle on each block's OWN prefab child set, since IsSea=0 ignores Donor.txt. title: Single-lobe size limit comes from the blob generator's 1/R turning, not from an FF9 law
claim: The shape gate encodes a scale-free stock fact: coasts turn a median ~22 deg per 8u at every size. blob_outline perturbs only frequencies f=2..5 with amplitude ~1/f, so its 8u turning falls as 1/R. Measured here: r24 median 24.1, r40 14.7, r60 9.8, r80 7.2 (0/20 seeds pass), r120 4.8. Every r>=80 single mass refuses, and even PASSING r60 islands are at 9.8 deg, less than half stock's 22, which makes them smoother than any stock coast. Large single landmasses, the owner's 'new landmass' case, are blocked by a generator gap that the gate only reports.
laws_involved: THE MASSING LAWS (the silhouette is the carrier)
evidence: mesh.py:1138-1162: blob_outline comps over f in (2,3,4,5), amplitude undulation*(...)/f, n=96 points. island.py:1144-1148: the gate 8<=med_turn<=35, acute<=0.12. Scratch shape.py: 20 seeds per radius as above.
proposed_action: Scale the outline detail with radius: add 8u-scale ripple harmonics (or corner count) proportional to R/24, and scale n with the perimeter, so median turn sits near 22 deg at any size. As a carry-first alternative, let build_landmass take a REAL stock coast polyline, transformed, as its outline. That carries the silhouette, which THE FORM LESSON names as the look carrier, while materials stay minted. The prefab frame would then need to admit custom outlines (today refused as 'unmeasured', island.py:452-454).
cheapest_test: Offline: sweep R 60-140 with the scaled ripple and require shape gate pass plus census MISS==0 and lip-streak 0 (verify_landmass). Then one owner walk of an r100 single-lobe mint next to an r60 control.
risk: More ripple means more short wall segments and sharper corners. The arc-length rock band and V-corner roles were proven on the gentle outlines, so wrap seams could show at tight turns. The acute <=12% and max-turn gates bound this, and the walk is the judge.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is right. blob_outline's undulation runs over f = 2..5 with amplitude ~1/f, so turning per 8u falls as 1/R. My re-run of shape.py matches: med_turn 24.1 / 14.7 / 9.8 / 7.2 / 5.7 / 4.8 at r24 / 40 / 60 / 80 / 100 / 120, with 0/20 passing at r>=80. But the symptom and the cure are already in the record. snowmassif/NOTES.md:17 and the terrain-malleability memory record 'a one-lobe outline over about r80 fails the shape gate: med_turn 7.3 < 8'. Round 21 worked around it with --lobes 2 at r88. The coast memory says multi_blob_outline added 'an 8u-scale ripple (big radii need it -- the same angular undulation turns gentler as radius grows)'. So 'large landmasses are blocked' is overstated. New, from my run: multi_blob_outline ALSO decays (lobes 2: p50 14.8 at r60, 10.7 at r88, 8.0 at r120 with only 10/20 passing), because its ripple is relative-angular too. The real open gap is a ripple scaled by absolute arc length for both generators. The carried-stock-polyline outline idea is new, but world-river already passes custom outlines.
citations: scratchpad r/shape.py (re-run) and my inline multi-lobe sweep
verdict.corrected_claim: The single-lobe outline gets smoother as 1/R and fails the shape gate past ~r80. That is known, and worked around with --lobes 2. The multi-lobe outline has the same falloff more slowly, reaching ~50% failure at r120. Very large landmasses need ripple scaled by absolute arc length in both generators, not just in the single-lobe one.

title: THE WALL-CONTEXT refusal of scrub/brush/dunes islands is really about ground meeting a crest, since their wall band IS the desert band

title: Dihedral prefab stamping: rotate the WRITTEN triangles 90/180/270 deg about a 64u lattice corner
claim: A quarter turn about a block corner maps the 64u block grid and the 4u cell lattice onto themselves. Block clipping therefore commutes with the turn, and the turned land needs no re-mint and no re-clip. Mains UV is linear in XZ with four rotations and ONE handedness, so a turned mains tri wears another of the four lawful rotations with the same handedness. The kit already places meadow stamps at rot 0/90/180/270 and carries massifs at any angle (owner-passed). There is no facing-baked light, and the overworld camera yaws freely, so a turned island shows the player the same set of views. Only the Sea4 cut, coastnav, Donor.txt and the disc-4 mirror are regenerated from the turned footprint; they are not rotated. Each walk then qualifies 4 orientations, and a non-square footprint turned 90 deg fits different windows. Self-rejected half: a MIRROR flips UV handedness, which stock never ships, and reverses the rock band's U sense.

title: Carry the SILHOUETTE: mint islands inside real stock coastline polylines
claim: THE FORM LESSON, refined, says massing and silhouette carry the look. The one silhouette the kit invents is the coast: blob_outline and multi_blob_outline are star-convex R(theta) curves with angular-frequency ripple. That rules out bays, hooks and C-shapes. It also means the 8u turn statistic falls as radius grows, so the shape gate refuses large single-mass islands. build_landmass already accepts a custom outline ring (inset along the normals; world-river uses it). The proposal: feed it real coast polylines (sea-ringed stock components, or continent stretches closed by a smooth seaward arc), rotated and translated, so the outline is real while the cliff band and mains stay the proven free tilings. The direction is the reverse of the banned hybrid: synthetic surface inside a real frame, not real content through a synthetic frame. It is also the prerequisite for bays (A4) and for large islands.
evidence: KIT FACT: blob_outline is single-valued R(theta) with f=2..5 undulation (mesh.py:1138-1162). multi_blob_outline's 'ripple' is angular f=9,13,17 (mesh.py:1190-1191), so its spatial wavelength grows with R. The shape gate needs med_turn >= 8 deg at a fixed 8u step (island.py:1144-1148). KIT FACT: the custom outline path uses _inset_ring (island.py:466-487). PLAYTEST VERDICT: world-river's custom-outline mint is owner-passed. STOCK CENSUS: real coasts turn a median 22 deg per 8u at every size (coast-mosaic shape language).
proposed_action: Add world-island --outline-from BX,BY[:component] --rot DEG, which takes the boundary ring of a stock land component (or a continent stretch plus a closing arc) and resamples it. Measure the prefab frame under a frame-relative outline, then lift the refusal for that case.
cheapest_test: Offline. Extract the boundary rings of the 23 sea-ringed stock components of 20-600 cells. Run build_landmass(outline=...) plus verify_landmass for each. Report the pass rate on the shape, clearance and inset self-intersection gates, and render 3 beside their stock originals at the game camera. Registered prediction: at least 80% pass the shape gate unmodified, because they ARE the census.
risk: A stock coast's 8u notches belong to its own lip, and minted over them they may read as noise. Tight concavities can self-intersect the inset ring. A recognisable stock island shape duplicated reads as a copy, so prefer continent stretches or turned or partial rings. The prefab frame is unmeasured for custom outlines.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. blob_outline is single-valued R(theta) and star-convex (mesh.py:1138-1146). multi_blob_outline is also kept star-convex, and its ripple is angular f=9,13,17, so its spatial wavelength does grow with R. build_landmass accepts a custom ring through _inset_ring (island.py:466-487), and world-river minted a non-blob ring derived from a stock fragment (a distance-transform contour), owner-passed. The prefab frame refuses custom outlines (island.py:441-443). No precedent exists for minting inside a stock coast polyline. Overstated: 'the shape gate refuses large single-mass islands' is not demonstrated. The kit already countered this with adaptive ring density past r60 and the 8u-scale ripple ('big radii need it'), and PREFABS plans an r88 two-lobe snow isle. The gate does fix the window at 8u-35 deg med turn (island.py:1145-1148). Risks hold: a 4u-cell component boundary must be resampled smoothly, and self-intersection of the inset at tight concavities is a real risk. The analyst's '80% pass' prediction is plausible but unregistered.

title: Cove carry: beaches on minted islands by generalising world-river's join columns, with no river needed

So FUSE's 'land never knits' is narrower than it is applied. The proposal is a CoveDonor: the stock beach arc plus its sand, foam and full water ladder, flooded seaward from the beach rather than from a river mouth. title: Relief-aware hosts: a detrended hill guard, and carries seated on rolling relief
claim: The kit's hosts are flat by default, and relief is documented as mutually exclusive with the relief verbs. The code enforces only the hill's 2.4u raw y-span test (interior.py:1386-1389), which cannot tell ambient relief from a prior hill. Stock features sit ON the regional ground field: a calm host is only about 10% of stock components (S5). The relief field is deterministic and frame-relative under the prefab frame, so the hill guard can test the RESIDUAL over grassland.relief at the same seed and frame. Forest and mountain carves already read the soup heights, so whether they seat on relief can simply be measured. The result is prefabs whose hosts sit in the 90% stock case, not the 10% one.
evidence: KIT POLICY: the 2.4u guard (interior.py:1386-1389) and the docstring 'MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE ... the 2.4u gate is the backstop' (island.py:390-393). STOCK CENSUS: 17/176 calm hosts (GROUND-JUNCTION-SYNTHESIS S5). PLAYTEST VERDICT: relief 'nice - gently rolling'. PLAYTEST VERDICT: flat interiors are also approved at r52 ('fine desert'). The gain is therefore context fidelity under carries, not a fix for a named defect. HEURISTIC (another reader's scratch sampling, unverified by me): about 22.5% of r20 footprints on amp-1.3 relief exceed 2.4u.
proposed_action: Change lawful() to test max |y - relief(x,z)| (or a local plane-fit residual) instead of the raw span. Allow relief on prefab islands with carries. Fix the stale grassland module docstring.
cheapest_test: Offline world-fuse: a framed relief island (amp 1.3) with a hill, a forest and the desert peak. Report every refusal and the apron slope stats. If they compose, register one A/B: the same carries on a flat vs a relief host, blind stills.
risk: The apron lift on relief may exceed the 29.5 deg apron envelope near the rim. relief_fade near the coast can interact with a carry close to the rim. The owner may not see the difference at prefab scale, as with the desert fidelity check.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. The hill guard is a raw y-span test (max-min > 2.4 refuses) over the footprint, and it cannot distinguish ambient relief from a prior hill (interior.py:1383-1389). island.py's docstring declares relief 'MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE' with the explicit-height verbs, with the 2.4u gate as the backstop (island.py:390-393). The grassland module docstring is stale: it still says relief was RETIRED while the module ships relief() at :656 and island.py calls it a resurrection. S5's calm-host figure is 17/176. The frame made relief anchor-relative (PREFABS P0). The payoff is context fidelity, not a named defect: flat interiors are owner-approved. The 22.5% figure is unverified, as the analyst says.
verdict.corrected_claim: The hill guard's raw 2.4u span conflates relief with prior displacement. A detrended residual test would let carries sit on framed relief hosts. This is fidelity work, not a defect fix, and it needs one registered A/B.

title: Room: count with the seams, read live occupancy instead of the stock bundle, and test the z seam

title: Blind decoy contact sheets plus an automated harness walk as the qualification oracle

LOOK: the harness shoots a fixed camera rig (4 azimuths x 2 distances) of N candidates AND K stock DECOYS (verbatim carried stock islands, the A5 units) placed in disjoint windows, or on 9013 where room is unlimited. Shuffle the stills into an unlabelled sheet. A candidate qualifies on look when the owner flags it no more often than the decoys. This calibrates the instrument the way CALIBRATE THE INSTRUMENT demands. It also removes the 'look at what changed' cue that may inflate THE DEFECT FOLLOWS THE AUTHORSHIP.

title: A calibrated offline look critic built on render_gate and the archived verdict corpus: rank and reject, never qualify
claim: render_gate.py is a faithful UNLIT software rasterizer (the engine binds no normal), and judged builds are archived in backups/ with their verdicts in the SCORED sections. A simple, interpretable metric can be fitted to that corpus. Candidates: the share of rendered 16px patches with no near match in a stock render bank at the same camera class, plus screen-space texel-density and anisotropy outliers along authored boundaries. Admit it only if (a) it separates held-out pass and fail rounds and (b) pure stock scores as pass (THE TRANSPLANT NULL). Use it only to prune A8 searches and order blind sheets. It must never become a new green gate.
laws_involved: A GREEN GATE SUITE IS A REGRESSION HARNESS, NOT AN ORACLE
evidence: KIT FACT: RENDER-GATE.md registered the instrument with the calibration law ('gates nothing until it reproduces the LAST rounds' defects offline'). Revised gate record: after the render and peer gates, 4 defects were caught offline and 2 found by the owner (SEGMENT-TRANSPLANT 'The gate record, honestly'). ENGINE FACT: Terrain renders from position plus uv0 only, so an unlit render is the engine's own model.
proposed_action: Assemble verdicts.csv (build path, camera, verdict, named defect) from the SCORED sections. Compute 2-3 metrics and report the AUC per arc.
cheapest_test: 10 pass and 10 fail archived builds that render_gate can already load. If the AUC on held-out arcs is below ~0.8, or pure stock scores as fail, drop the critic.
risk: With n of about 40 verdicts over diverse defect classes, the critic will overfit. Some archived builds may not be recoverable. The Moguri gutter smear is invisible to an offline sampler that skips transparent texels, so the critic must sample gutters as white.

verdict.reason: The analyst understates what exists. RENDER-GATE.md did not merely 'register' the instrument. Its calibration predictions P-A..P-E all scored ('the gate is LIVE'), and a close-range upgrade later passed calibration too. A PEER GATE (probe_peer_compare.py) already compares a candidate against owner-approved peers at identically placed cameras, which is most of A11's 'no near match in a reference bank' idea, and SEGMENT-TRANSPLANT credits it with 4 offline catches. The new part is a corpus-fitted metric with held-out AUC across arcs, plus the transplant-null check. The analyst's own n of about 40 overfitting risk is the binding constraint.
citations: studies/path-d-new-world/RENDER-GATE.md:6-8, :93-125 (calibration all PASS, gate LIVE), :127-145 (close-range calibration PASS)
verdict.corrected_claim: render_gate is calibrated and live, and a peer-comparison gate against owner-approved renders already exists. A11 reduces to fitting and held-out-testing a cross-arc ranking metric on the archived verdicts, used only to prune and order candidates.

title: Re-run THE ONE-SITE WORLD LAW scan on the reset map with the seam allowed
claim: 'The map holds exactly one landmass of this class' (CLAUDE.md section 10; PREFABS max_per_world = 1) is an occupancy enumeration from 2026-07-25. The scan also counted live benches, and the 2026-11 reset removed all of them, Rung F included. The law's premises are stale. A second two-ground landmass (the most varied composition the kit has, 36 gates and site-independent) may fit, and on 9013 the law does not apply at all.
laws_involved: THE WORLD IS A FULL TORUS
evidence: STOCK CENSUS (stale): freshmint_site_scan.py docstring (c) 'build_landmass REFUSES col<0'. The best other site was 115.38u vs 125.38u needed (GROUND-FAMILY-DECODE:2418). KIT FACT: island.py:870-897 wraps columns now. PREFABS.md P2: after the reset 'all 30 stock windows free'. PLAYTEST VERDICT: junction_compose carried into 9013 'looks identical'.

verdict.reason: The scan's seam exclusion is confirmed stale. freshmint_site_scan.py docstring (c) says 'build_landmass REFUSES col<0', and columns now wrap (island.py:866-897). The occupancy premise is subtler than claimed. The law said the STOCK world holds exactly one R>=125 site (the Rung F site), 'now occupied by its own island', and that the best other site is 115.38u, and the law itself names 'a de-deployed bench' as the escape. The reset moved every disc-1 land edit to backups, so that one site is likely free again, but off-seam the count is still one. Only the seam wrap could add sites. max_per_world = 1 is a PREFABS.md proposal, not code (no hits in the package). The 9013 escape is currently unavailable, because 9013 was unregistered by the reset.
verdict.corrected_claim: THE ONE-SITE WORLD LAW is a stock-clearance enumeration with the seam excluded. The reset most likely re-frees its one off-seam site but does not add a second. Re-running the scan with wrapped columns is the only open lever. max_per_world is a doc proposal, and 9013 needs restoring before it can be an escape.

title: A mid-water halo for minted islands, built only from the proven open-ocean alphabet
claim: world-island ships only the pure-deep water context: HIDDEN_PARTS blanks Sea1/2/3/5, and the Uaho Donor.txt default is itself ~98% deep-fronted. A read-only census over 23 small sea-ringed stock islands found the deep context in only 6. Seven are at least 90% mid-fronted (sea3/sea5) and the rest mixed. A sea3/sea5 halo whose depth field is distance-to-outline, emitted by world-water's in-game-proven marching band, uses no shallow (sea1/sea2) synthesis. It never puts sea3 against sea4, by construction. It gives each prefab a second water dress, and that dress is the commonest stock context.
laws_involved: THE RING LADDER + LATTICE ADJACENCY LAW
evidence: STOCK CENSUS (heuristic, scratch): first_water.json (6 of 23 pure deep, 7 of 23 mid). KIT FACT: island.py:51-53 (HIDDEN_PARTS), :71-72. PLAYTEST VERDICT: world-water in game 'looks good', 17/17 shape match. STOCK CENSUS: 13 of 15 stock water-only blocks carry exactly such sea3/sea5 shoals.
proposed_action: Add world-island --halo mid --halo-width W(theta), a smooth width field. Choose a Donor.txt whose prefab exposes Sea3 and Sea5. Re-cut Sea4 disjoint from the halo coverage.
cheapest_test: Offline: list donor prefabs exposing Sea3+Sea5 (extract.block_parts). Build the halo on desert-peak-isle in a scratch folder. Run texgates sea-plan-disjoint plus the ladder adjacency check plus render_gate. One blind still against a mid-haloed stock island ((12,15) or (17,9)).
risk: The halo is new authored surface: water in a free tiling, but its SHAPE reads (stock widths track bathymetry). Coplanar layers z-fight if coverage overlaps. Changing the Donor.txt prefab may change which other parts free-ride.

verdict.reason: Mechanism confirmed. HIDDEN_PARTS blanks Sea1/2/3/5 (island.py:51). world-water's marching band uses only Sea3/Sea5/Sea4, never lets Sea3 touch Sea4, and is in-game proven at 17/17 (water.py:1-30). Coast-mosaic memory says a custom water body in open ocean must be deep at its outer rim with mid inside, which the band satisfies. The census numbers are off when re-read from the scratch file. Of the 23 components of 20-600 cells, 5 (not 6) are at least 90% deep-fronted (4 purely deep) and 5 (not 7) are at least 90% mid-fronted. Map-wide, lip58 first water is sea4 2752 against sea3 2169 and sea5 240, so mid fronting is common but not dominant. Uaho (0,0) is 0.983 deep, as claimed. Note too that the island's donor prefab presumably already exposes Sea3/Sea5, since they are blanked, so a donor change may be unnecessary.
verdict.corrected_claim: A Sea3/Sea5 halo from world-water's proven marching band is a lawful second water dress. About 5 of 23 small stock islands are mostly mid-fronted, 5 are mostly deep-fronted, and the rest are mixed. Its shape is new authored surface and needs one blind comparison.

title: Smooth declared non-uniform maps for carried relief: anisotropic spread first, then a low-order taper
claim: The record's real boundary is not 'never move carried bytes'. It is SMOOTH GLOBAL DECLARED maps (rotation, uniform spread to x1.5, pure-Y to x2, the de-tilt shear: all passed) against LOCAL per-vertex pulls (the blend conform, the v3 bend-carry's ribbon plus fix-ups: failed). The rock-rigid gate already measures drift against the DECLARED shape, so an anisotropic plan scale (sx != sz) or a linear taper fits the existing machinery with no new gate logic. Seven massifs then become a continuous family of footprints (long ridges, squat domes) without inventing massing.
laws_involved: real content through a synthetic frame (section 8)
evidence: PLAYTEST VERDICT: --spread x1.5 'B, C and D all read as stock mountains'; the v1/v2 blend conform 'stays refuted (an uneven, rim-driven per-vertex pull, not a height scale)' (RESULTS.md:1008). HEURISTIC: plan shear 0.25 survival is ~96% for every class (uvclass table). KIT FACT: MTN_ROCK_RIGID is measured against the declared map (interior.py:135-137). SYNTHESIS-RECONSIDERED: the section 8 line 'forbids the one hybrid that works'.
proposed_action: Add --spread-x/--spread-z (each 1.0-1.5) to world-mountain and world-forest. Defer a taper or bend until the anisotropic case is passed.
cheapest_test: Offline uvc_deform survival on Uaho at (1.0, 1.4) and (1.4, 1.0). Then one blind still panel (isotropic 1.2 vs anisotropic 1.0/1.4).
risk: Anisotropy distorts the silhouette, which carries the look, so it may read as 'stretched' sooner than uniform scale. The apron and zip must still seat. Payoff overlaps A6 and A2.

verdict.reason: The distinction is well grounded. Passed: smooth declared global maps (spread x1.5, pure-Y x2, rotation). Refuted: the v1/v2 blend conform, an 'uneven, rim-driven per-vertex pull' (RESULTS.md:1008). MTN_ROCK_RIGID measures drift against the DECLARED shape (interior.py:135-137), so an anisotropic declared map fits the existing gate. Plan shear 0.25 keeps about 96% survival in every class. SYNTHESIS-RECONSIDERED does say the section 8 line 'forbids the one hybrid that works' (rigid carry in a minted frame). No anisotropic-spread precedent was found. The silhouette risk is the right one to flag, because the FORM LESSON makes the silhouette the carrier.
verdict.corrected_claim: --spread-x/--spread-z (1.0-1.5) is a smooth declared map that the rock-rigid gate already handles. It is untested, and the binding risk is a visibly stretched silhouette.

title: A law-scope register cited at every refusal, plus fixes to the over-broad lines it would surface
claim: Several restrictions are applied beyond their measured scope, and nothing in code knows that. Examples: CLAUDE.md section 8's 'real content through a synthetic frame' line; ONE-SITE stated as permanent; shallows as 'copy-only' while the kit emits sea1/sea2 at shores in game; the Uaho-only ceilings applied to all donors; WALL-CONTEXT refusing on Path D, where SYNTHESIS-RECONSIDERED calls it a design choice; the stock-probe open-ocean proxy; edged-z. Two adjacency tables also disagree outright: transplant.SEA_ADJ_LAWFUL admits sea2|sea3 (9 stock instances) and coastmorph._LAWFUL_ADJ omits it. 'A law in a docstring is a wish': give each law an id, a kind, a measured scope and its call sites. Make every refusal name its law id, and add a test that flags any 'policy' or 'extrapolated' law gating a scope it was not measured on. Separately, adopt the candidate generation law the record supports but never states: synthesize a seam only from vocabulary measured on the element it JOINS (the TUCK and the join column passed; the map-wide-constant fairing and the curtain mint failed).
laws_involved: section 8 'real content through a synthetic frame'
evidence: KIT FACT: transplant.py:2651-2660 vs coastmorph.py:3877-3880 (verified). KIT FACT: grassland.py:18-28 still says relief is RETIRED while the same file ships relief(). KIT POLICY: island.py:427-444 refuses WALL-CONTEXT with no disc exception. SYNTHESIS-RECONSIDERED: 'The section 8 line as written forbids the one hybrid that works'. PLAYTEST VERDICT: the TUCK passed (SEGMENT-TRANSPLANT playtest 12); fairing v2 failed through green gates (VSHORE-SEAL playtest 6).
proposed_action: Create world/data/laws.toml and a world-laws --why CLI. Re-census sea2|sea3 to settle the table conflict. Propose (owner-confirm) CLAUDE.md wording: section 8 'WARPED real content ... (rigid or smooth-declared carries in a minted frame pass)'; section 10 ONE-SITE scoped to 'July occupancy, one donor size'. Add a disc-scoped override for painted-grammar laws (WALL-CONTEXT, home ground) behind an explicit flag on a synthetic disc.
cheapest_test: Tabulate the ~30 laws in these maps with their measured vs applied scope, and count how many gate a scope they were not measured on. Re-census sea2|sea3 edges map-wide: are the 9 instances systematic or one block's dialect?
risk: Relaxing a fail-closed gate on a scope argument alone is how silent bricks happen (the dunes off-grid write, bad geometry under the spawn). Relaxations must still pass through one registered test each. Editing CLAUDE.md is the owner's call.

verdict.reason: The table conflict is real but should not be called an outright contradiction. transplant.SEA_ADJ_LAWFUL admits sea2|sea3 (9 instances) and coastmorph._LAWFUL_ADJ omits it. However, they come from different censuses with different scopes. transplant's is directed-edge, land-aware and cross-block, and gates crops. coastmorph's is owner-cell 4-adjacency (2026-07-11) and gates band conversion. coastmorph also lists sea3|sea5 and sea5|sea4, which transplant handles separately. The grassland docstring staleness is confirmed (grassland.py:17-26 vs relief() at :656 and island.py:384-391). WALL-CONTEXT refuses with no disc exception (island.py:425-444), but it is MEASURED for canyon, scrub and dunes, and its blind spot (adjacency within a block's own tris only) is recorded in memory. The section 8 critique is confirmed by SYNTHESIS-RECONSIDERED. The claim that the kit emits sea1/sea2 at shores in game was not verified. The proposal (a law-scope register, with refusals citing law ids) is a sound kit-policy idea. Changing CLAUDE.md is the owner's call.
verdict.corrected_claim: Several laws are applied beyond their measured scope, and the grassland docstring is stale. The two sea-adjacency tables differ because they come from different census methods for different gates. They need reconciling (re-census sea2|sea3), but they are not simply contradictory. WALL-CONTEXT is measured, not assumed, for canyon, scrub and dunes.

title: Sub-block placement by rigid translate-and-repartition, judged by a surface fingerprint
claim: 'A 4u or 32u shift gives different land' was measured by RE-RUNNING the mint at a shifted centre and comparing TRIANGLES. A rigid 0-mod-4 translation of the already-written triangles, re-clipped at the new 64u block lines, keeps the same piecewise-linear surface. The new clip lines are lattice lines, so split mains tris stay inside their cell windows and the UVs interpolate exactly. A surface fingerprint (position+uv sampled on a dense grid plus the walk census) then shows whether the land is the same. That would give 256 offsets per block for the editor's nudge and for fitting into tight windows, while one walk still covers them.
evidence: KIT POLICY: PREFABS.md table rows '4u, 32u: different land (the block/cell clip moves)'; the measurement re-ran build_landmass. KIT FACT: the fingerprint hashes triangles (prefab.py:167-188). STOCK CENSUS: L.rule '0-mod-4 exact' (uvclass LAWFUL DEFORMATIONS). ENGINE FACT: new cut lines inside a tri are fine for render, but a vertex exactly on a split edge is the barycentric teleport-trap class.
proposed_action: Add prefab.place(..., nudge=(dx,dz)) with dx,dz in multiples of 4u. Translate the staged soup, re-partition at block lines, re-cut Sea4, compare by surface sampling rather than triangle multiset, and keep a whole-block identity record alongside.
cheapest_test: Offline: take desert-peak-isle's staged output, translate by (4,0) and (32,0), re-clip, and sample position+uv on a 0.5u grid plus the offline walk census, against the unshifted output translated in the sampler. Any difference beyond float32 noise falsifies this.
risk: The Sea4 cut, Donor.txt and coastnav are per-block and must be regenerated. Extra cut vertices add T-junction or teleport-trap exposure. Low payoff while room is set by whole windows.

verdict.reason: The premise is confirmed. PREFABS.md's '4u, 32u: different land' row was measured by RE-RUNNING build_landmass at a shifted centre, and the fingerprint hashes triangles (prefab.py:167-188), so a re-partitioned translate would fail it by construction. uvclass gives L.rule '0-mod-4 exact' translation, and transplant runs 0-mod-4 shifts. The claim that a translated-and-reclipped soup is the same surface is plausible but unmeasured. Several per-block artefacts were built around the OLD block lines and would end up mid-block: the apron taper at block borders (interior.py:2566-2571) and the per-block Sea4/coastnav/Donor.txt. New cut vertices on split edges add teleport-trap exposure. Payoff is low while room is set by whole windows.
verdict.corrected_claim: Sub-block placement by rigid 0-mod-4 translate-and-repartition is a reasonable but unmeasured hypothesis, and it needs a surface (not triangle) fingerprint. Border-tapered aprons and per-block sidecars would be misplaced. Low payoff.

title: Ideas considered and REJECTED (or deferred), with the reason each falls into a known failure mode
claim: (1) MORPHING between two stock massifs: any intermediate needs blended UV charts. That synthesizes texture organization (M.flow/M.free), which is exactly THE FORM LESSON's measured class. Rejected. (2) STOCK-AS-TEXTURE REPROJECTION onto new massing: per-cell Terrain PNGs are clobbered by SetupPreloadedMaterials while a loose atlas exists (engine fact; X4 would need a DLL patch). The atlas has only ~124 free 32px cells. And the refined FORM LESSON says invented massing fails even with correct tiles. Deferred until a massing decode exists. (3) MIRRORED prefabs: these flip mains UV handedness, which stock never ships (see A2). Rejected. (4) SHRUNK DUNES to beat the size class: dunes are an L.rule mains family (+/-10%). Rejected (see A6). (5) DESERT/SNOW secondary-vocabulary stamps (desert mints are 100% mains vs stock ~32%): the owner already judged the gap invisible at r52 ('no and no -- this looks like a fine desert'). Low payoff; revisit only if a large desert prefab reads too regular. (6) CANYON/SCRUB/BRUSH islands: WALL-CONTEXT is MEASURED here (canyon 0 open-sea faces; scrub and brush one face each), not merely absent. Only canyon interior behind a carried topo-49 coast is lawful, and that needs an undecoded canyon|coast-family junction (the RIBBON FALLACY class). Deferred. (7) A REGISTERED RE-TEST of a synthetic massif face with today's foot laws: it is the one untested cell, but THE DEFECT FOLLOWS THE AUTHORSHIP predicts the defect lands on the face, and A1/A8/A14 reach bigger and varied relief with zero authored rock. Deferred. (8) A LEARNED deep 'looks-stock' network: about 40 verdicts cannot train it. Replaced by A11's interpretable metric.
laws_involved: PER-CELL TERRAIN TEXTURE OVERRIDE IS CLOBBERED
evidence: ENGINE FACT: WMWorld.cs:808 vs :842-846 clobber (consumption/NOTES.md section 5; uvclass X4 unrun). PLAYTEST VERDICT: the desert fidelity check closed 'no and no' (memory project-ff9-overworld-interior-topography.md, THE DESERT GROUND LANGUAGE study). STOCK CENSUS: uvclass rock49 M.flow 71.1%, Uaho 77.9% M.free. KIT FACT: island.py:427-444 refusal. PLAYTEST VERDICT: TERRACE-WALL round 2 refuted the tile-language discriminant.
proposed_action: Do not pursue (1), (3), (4) or (8). Park (2), (6) and (7) with the stated preconditions: a massing decode, a canyon junction census, and a fresh prediction registration.
cheapest_test: None required. For (7), if ever resumed: register the prediction first, and build only on a bench where the foot is carried (A1) so the face is the sole authored variable.
risk: Rejecting (7) outright could leave the owner's goal of truly new mountain SHAPES unmet if A14 and A8 prove too repetitive. Revisit after A8's search shows how much variety composition alone buys.

verdict.reason: Most of the rejections are well founded. (2) The per-cell Terrain PNG clobber is confirmed (consumption NOTES section 5: SetupPreloadedMaterials reassigns when loose textures exist; MoguriMain ships them). (5) The desert check closed with 'no and no -- this looks like a fine desert'. (6) WALL-CONTEXT is measured: scrub touches topo-58 once map-wide, dunes zero, brush deliberately unset. (1)/(7) follow THE FORM LESSON and the terrace-wall refutation. Two corrections. For (3), 'stock never ships mirror' holds for grass MAINS (one handedness), but stock rock-wall tiles include 12% mirrors (TERRACE-WALL round 2). Mains are L.rule and re-derivable by rule. A mirrored prefab therefore fails only on its carried M-class rock (whose mirror tolerance is unmeasured), not on the mains. For (6), the WALL-CONTEXT census only sees adjacency within a block's own triangle list, a recorded blind spot, so 'measured' carries that caveat.
citations: memory project-ff9-overworld-interior-topography.md:837 (desert 'no and no'), :1158-1170 (scrub/dunes/brush wall_coastal + blind spot)
verdict.corrected_claim: The rejections hold, with two caveats. The mirror rejection applies to mains UV handedness and to carried rock of unmeasured mirror tolerance. Mains could be re-derived by rule, and stock walls do mirror. WALL-CONTEXT's measurements share the within-block adjacency blind spot.
